Governance As compared to PD, higher proportion of respondents from NPD was involved in district plan preparation (NPD = 78.9 % vs. PD = 58.5 %) and trained in preparing the plan (NPD = 47.4 % vs. PD = 27.5 %). On the other hand, the findings were converse for variables, such as, participation of representatives from other departments (PD = 96.9 % vs. NPD = 45.5 %), inclusion of activities of other sectors (PD = 70.8 % vs. NPD = 41.8 %) and regular review of the progress (PD = 85.7 % vs. NPD = 90.2 %). All the above mentioned differences were statistically significant. Nine out of 49 respondents in PD and 6 out Table 1 Opinion, perception and practices related to governance

On further probing about what they had included as ‘different’ than ‘local priorities’, only 4 from PD and 2 from NPD responded. Fluorosis control, malaria and dengue con- trol, provision to address water shortage and manage- ment of malnutrition were cited as the special programs.
